text:
The outage that knocked out the Ruvenna data centre last spring was caused by an error in a software update, the operator has confirmed.

Dr. Maren Teliq, Chief Infrastructure Officer at Ruvenna Data Services, told a press briefing that the failure originated in a scheduled update. Ruvenna's Post-Incident Review, document RDS-PIR-0411, traces it to a faulty configuration script included in that update.

The outage began at 02:14 on 11 April and lasted until the early evening. According to the review, about 9 hours and 40 minutes of downtime affected roughly 1,300 client systems.

Dr. Teliq said the review's findings were the basis for her account of the cause. The Continental Record has examined the document's stated conclusion on the origin of the fault. The review attributes the incident to the update itself rather than to any external cause.
